concepts.title: Chemical Reaction
concepts.ncert_text: A process where substances (reactants) transform into new substances (products) with different properties. Accompanied by change in state, color, gas evolution, or temperature change.

concepts.title: Law of Conservation of Mass
concepts.ncert_text: Mass can neither be created nor destroyed in a chemical reaction. The total mass of elements in products must equal the total mass in reactants. Equations must be balanced.

concepts.title: Combination Reaction
concepts.ncert_text: A reaction in which a single product is formed from two or more reactants. Example: CaO(s) + H2O(l) -> Ca(OH)2(aq) + Heat.

concepts.title: Decomposition Reaction
concepts.ncert_text: A single reactant breaks down to give simpler products. Requires energy in form of heat (thermal), light (photolytic), or electricity (electrolytic).

concepts.title: Displacement Reaction
concepts.ncert_text: A reaction where a more reactive element displaces a less reactive element from its compound. Example: Fe(s) + CuSO4(aq) -> FeSO4(aq) + Cu(s).

concepts.title: Redox Reaction
concepts.ncert_text: If a substance gains oxygen or loses hydrogen during a reaction, it is oxidized. If it loses oxygen or gains hydrogen, it is reduced. Both occur simultaneously in Redox reactions.

concepts.title: Corrosion and Rancidity
concepts.ncert_text: Corrosion: Deterioration of metals by action of air/moisture (e.g., rusting). Rancidity: Oxidation of fats and oils in food making them smell/taste bad.
